title: Digital Innovation and Product Development Capability
problemSolved: King’s does not yet have a sustained multidisciplinary team or consistent product practices for moving emerging student-experience needs from discovery and prototype into secure, supported institutional operation.
whatChanges: King’s establishes a lean four-person multidisciplinary digital product core to deliver King’s Edge and the focused first Digital Student Experience Hub release while testing the capability model itself. Following the 28 August 2026 Digital and IT alignment conversation, the Year One planning shape is a senior backend/integration or architecture-capable engineer, a middleweight full-stack engineer, a full-time product/UX/UI designer and a dedicated QA engineer, with the exact split between senior engineering and solution architecture to be confirmed by Digital and IT. Product ownership, delivery coordination, DevOps and specialist architecture, data, integration, security, accessibility and service-management input are supplied through named existing or shared capability where feasible. Protected service-design, business-analysis and user-research capacity remains additional to the build pod. Agentic software-development tooling is treated as an accelerator for an experienced team rather than a substitute for engineering judgement. Evidence from delivery and discovery then determines the enduring team shape and any future expansion.

decisionLog.forum: Student Experience Hub strategic alignment review
decisionLog.outcome: Confirmed that the 4.0 FTE funded product pod remains the Year One core. Broad digital-estate mapping and student-journey discovery require additional named and protected service-design and business-analysis capacity, with reliable user-research support. The planning assumption is to secure this through existing or seconded institutional capability where possible, without tying it to a particular organisational home or automatically enlarging the permanent pod. Specialist technical and assurance inputs remain time-bound and should be explicitly protected when needed.

decisionLog.forum: Digital Experience Hub alignment conversation with Digital and IT
decisionLog.outcome: Revised the Year One four-person product-core hypothesis. The working staffing shape is one senior backend/integration or solution-architecture-capable engineer, one middleweight full-stack engineer, one full-time product/UX/UI designer and one dedicated QA engineer, with QA potentially starting later once code production is established. Digital and IT will confirm whether the senior engineering role can also cover solution architecture or whether architecture must be supplied separately.

decisionLog.forum: Digital Experience Hub alignment conversation with Digital and IT
decisionLog.outcome: Confirmed the mobilisation route: Education secures the investment through the strategic funding process and Digital and IT creates and recruits the technical roles through its workforce processes. The existing KAI team will not be transferred wholesale into the Hub capability, although reusable technical assets should be assessed deliberately, including Azure AI Foundry components.

decisionLog.forum: Digital Experience Hub alignment conversation with Digital and IT
decisionLog.outcome: Agentic software development should be incorporated into the Year One delivery model as an accelerator used by an experienced engineering team. A separate project-level tooling allowance should be costed provisionally and validated by Digital and IT rather than assumed to replace core engineering capacity.
